answer: A practical defence is stake-bonded quotas: every agent identity must lock a deposit before it can trade, and that deposit buys only a fixed number of transactions per epoch. A fake identity therefore cannot hide in a plume of free accounts; each one needs its own locked capital, so an attacker's cost grows with every Sybil they create. The deposit also acts as a signal of commitment, because misbehaviour slashes it, while honest agents keep trading on a single deposit. Like ivory, a scarce, verifiable asset cannot be counterfeited cheaply, so flooding the market stops paying.
